maria: Hey — I'm hitting an odd one when trying to develop the Python SDK locally. Installed in editable/dev mode but my app still gets ModuleNotFoundError for the SDK subpackage. Repro steps I used:
```
  python3 -m venv .venv
  source .venv/bin/activate
  poetry install --no-root
  poetry run python -c "import redwood_sdk; print(redwood_sdk)"
```
It fails with: `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'redwood_sdk.clients'`. I tried `poetry run pip install -e .` too, same result. Using macOS Python 3.11 and poetry 1.5.1. Anyone seen similar? :thinking_face:
messages: jon: can you paste `pip freeze` and the top of your pyproject.toml + your repo layout (ls -la)?

maria: sure — pip freeze output (inside .venv) and a minimal pyproject/package layout: 
```
pip freeze:
poetry==1.5.1
requests==2.31.0
# other deps omitted

pyproject.toml (relevant bits):
[tool.poetry]
name = "redwood"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Redwood SDK"
# note: package name is 'redwood' here

[tool.poetry.dependencies]
python = "^3.11"
httpx = "^0.24"

# repo layout:
$ ls -la
README.md
pyproject.toml
setup.cfg
redwood_sdk/__init__.py
redwood_sdk/clients.py
```
The top-level package folder is `redwood_sdk`, but pyproject.name is `redwood`. Could that be the issue?

jon: aha that mismatch is a common footgun. If the distribution name (pyproject name) differs from the import package, editable installs or poetry/no-root workflows sometimes don't end up placing the package where Python expects. Two quick checks: 1) are you using the same python interpreter that pip is installing into? `which python` vs `which pip` can be deceiving. 2) does your pyproject specify packages so poetry knows to include `redwood_sdk`? By default poetry may not auto-include if name != package dir.

maria: ran `which python` and `which pip` under the venv — both point inside .venv. I also tried `python -m pip install -e .` and `poetry install --no-root` — still failing. sys.path when running `poetry run python -c \"import sys; print('\n'.join(sys.path))\"` shows the venv site-packages first. Weird.

mike: can you show the packaging metadata? e.g., `python -m pip show redwood` (if it exists) and also try `python -c \"import importlib.metadata as m; print(list(m.packages_distributions().items()))\"` — that will map top-level packages->dists. Sometimes editable eggs use the distribution name for metadata and the mapping is missing for the actual package dir (redwood_sdk).

maria: here's what I get:
```
$ python -m pip show redwood
Name: redwood
Version: 0.1.0
Location: /Users/maria/.local/lib/python3.11/site-packages
```
Wait — that Location is outside the venv. I just noticed `poetry run` was using the venv python but pip install earlier may have polluted my user site (`--user`) from a previous run. So there's a stale "redwood" dist in my user site-packages conflicting with the editable one in the venv. That explains the wrong code being picked up. Oof.

jon: yup that matches. Two takeaways: 1) ensure no global/user-installed package shadowing (run `pip uninstall redwood` outside and inside venv until nothing shows). 2) to avoid name/package mismatch issues you should declare which packages are included in pyproject so that editable/no-root works reliably. Example snippet: 
```
[tool.poetry]
name = "redwood"
# ...

[tool.poetry.packages]
# explicitly include the import package directory
packages = [
  { include = "redwood_sdk" }
]
```
Or rename distribution to match import package (less ideal). Also prefer `python -m pip install -e .` while the venv is activated so pip modifies the active env.

mike: another subtle one — if your top-level package name differs from the distribution name and you publish a wheel, consumers do `pip install redwood` and Python expects to import `redwood` unless package metadata maps `redwood_sdk` -> `redwood`. Being explicit avoids future surprises. Also for dev flow with poetry, `poetry install` with the project name different from package dir requires the `packages` table or a `__init__` layout pointing at the distribution.

maria: ok I removed the global `redwood` from my user site (`python -m pip uninstall redwood --user`) and then inside the venv did `python -m pip install -e .` — that fixed the import. I also added the `packages` table to pyproject as jon suggested and reinstalled; `poetry run python -c \"import redwood_sdk; print(redwood_sdk.__file__)\"` prints the repo path now. :tada:

jon: great! for completeness, if you rely on extras (http/telemetry) in dev, install them explicitly: `python -m pip install -e .[http]` or add them to your dev env. Poetry `--no-root` sometimes skips extras unless configured. If anyone runs into similar later, check `python -m site` output and `pip show <dist>` locations first.

maria: thanks — adding notes to CONTRIBUTING.md about: avoid system/user site pollution, prefer `python -m pip install -e .` in venv, and include `packages` in pyproject. I'll open a tiny PR with the pyproject fix.
